title: Life in Biblical Israel
author: Philip J. King; Lawrence E. Stager
allowedUseNotes: Copyrighted monograph. Summaries in project's own words only.
summary: Synthesis of Israelite daily life and material culture: houses and construction, dress and textiles, food production, water systems, tools, and household organization. Primary anchor for material-culture claims (mudbrick construction, dress, wells, household scale). The book is organized around named topical sections including 'Foodways' (diet, nutrition, cooking, eating, feasting, and fasting) and 'Death ways' (mourning practices and mortuary ritual, within a broader 'Religious ways' treatment of tombs/the afterlife/the cult of the dead) — confirmed via the publisher's own chapter/section outline, not just general-subject inference. Researcher pass (2026-08-08, M5 citation-gap closure): this project cites the Foodways material as general (not Hebron-specific) comparative-ane corroboration that ordinary Iron Age Israelite communal eating was floor/mat-level with shared vessels rather than furniture-based banqueting — no distinct dedicated feast-hall architecture or reconstructed table-and-chair furniture is attested for this period and setting — supporting hebron-covenant's already-modeled modest open-air meal (claim-feast-form). The Death ways material is the same general mourning-and-mortuary-ritual anchor already used for claim-mourning-dress (torn clothes, sackcloth, dust) and is extended here to claim-abner-funeral's funeral-procession/burial staging as the same general convention, not a Hebron-specific or Abner-specific finding.
